record.original_question: For the van der Corput sequence in base 2, where a_n is obtained by writing n in base 2, reversing the digits, and interpreting the result as a real number in [0,1], build the associated 4-regular graph from the first N distinct terms using adjacency in original order and in sorted order. Give a rigorous explanation of the highly nontrivial structure that these graphs exhibit, rather than only the empirical pictures reported in the paper.

evidence.quote: The van der Corput sequence (in base 2) is another classical object in discrete mathematics. Its definition is somewhat whimsical: the element a_n is obtained by writing n in base 2, then reversing the order of the digits and then interpreting the resulting element as a real in [0, 1].
The arising graphs were already discussed in [19] and seem to have interesting and highly nontrivial structure, we refer to Fig. 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the van der Corput sequence in base 2 as follows: for each positive integer n with binary expansion n = sum_{k>=0} b_k 2^k (b_k in {0,1}), set
  a_n = sum_{k>=0} b_k 2^{-(k+1)} in [0,1].
For a fixed integer N >= 1, consider the first N terms a_1, a_2, ..., a_N (which are pairwise distinct). Let pi be the permutation of {1,...,N} for which a_{pi(1)} < a_{pi(2)} < ... < a_{pi(N)} (the sorted order). Build the "sequence graph" G_N on vertex set {1,...,N} by joining, for each i, the vertex i to its two neighbors in the original order (i-1 and i+1, when they exist) and to its two neighbors in the sorted order (pi(j-1) and pi(j+1) when pi(j)=i). Apart from a bounded number of low-degree vertices near the ends, G_N is 4-regular.

Problem: Give a rigorous description and proof of the asymptotic combinatorial / geometric structure of the family of graphs {G_N}_{N>=1} arising from the base-2 van der Corput sequence. In particular, identify and prove the structural features observed empirically (e.g., regular block patterns, embeddings into a specific surface, automorphism/recursion properties), going beyond numerical pictures to a complete theorem describing G_N for all N.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 preprint shows that the 4-regular graphs built from the base-2 van der Corput sequence embed into the Chamanara translation surface (up to possible removal of one edge), giving a structural geometric explanation. Earlier work by Korssjoen, Li, Steinerberger, Tripathi and Zhang catalogued empirical features. A complete rigorous description of the full combinatorial structure of these graphs does not yet appear to be established, but substantial progress has been made.

status_evidence.title: Obtaining the Chamanara Surface from the van der Corput sequence
status_evidence.snippet: The graphs constructed from the binary van der Corput sequence can be embedded into the Chamanara surface, with the possible removal of one edge.
status_evidence.claim: Structural identification of the van der Corput sequence graphs via embedding into the Chamanara translation surface.

status_evidence.title: Finding structure in sequences of real numbers via graph theory: a problem list
status_evidence.snippet: The arising graphs ... seem to have interesting and highly nontrivial structure.
status_evidence.claim: The structural problem for van der Corput sequence graphs was posed as open.
